name: Memory-R1: Enhancing Large Language Model Agents to Manage and Utilize Memories via Reinforcement Learning
venue: arXiv preprint (arXiv:2508.19828, cs.CL / cs.MA); submitted 27 Aug 2025, last revised 14 Jan 2026 (v5); no peer-reviewed venue confirmed as of this writing
authors_affiliation: Sikuan Yan, Xiufeng Yang (co-first authors), Zuchao Huang, Ercong Nie, Zifeng Ding, Zonggen Li, Xiaowen Ma, Jinhe Bi, Kristian Kersting, Jeff Z. Pan, Hinrich Schuetze, Volker Tresp, Yunpu Ma (corresponding). Primary affiliations: Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich (LMU) and Munich Center for Machine Learning; also Technical University of Munich, University of Cambridge, University of Hong Kong, Technical University of Darmstadt, University of Edinburgh.
code_url: [uncertain] No official standalone code repository was located; the paper does not advertise a GitHub link in v5. The method is listed/cited in the third-party survey repo https://github.com/elvin-yiming-du/survey_memory_in_ai but that is not the authors' code release.
task_domain: QA / decision-making over long-horizon multi-session dialogue memory (memory management + memory-augmented question answering); framed as a multi-agent system (cs.MA). Memory operations are cast as RL decision-making.
problem_setting: Interactive multi-session dialogue setting where each dialogue contains multiple sessions and turns, and answering a question requires synthesizing information spread across sessions. Two specialized agents (a Memory Manager and an Answer Agent) are fine-tuned with outcome-driven RL. Supervision is minimal: no per-operation labels are provided; only final-answer correctness (Exact Match against gold QA) acts as the learning signal, with only 152 training QA pairs. The two agents are trained separately (decoupled) for stability under sparse rewards; when training one agent the other is frozen.
what_is_retrieved: Episodic memory entries (natural-language fact statements / consolidated memories) distilled from prior dialogue turns and stored in an external memory bank; at QA time a set of candidate memory entries is retrieved via similarity-based RAG.
retrieval_grounding: GROWING/episodic memory the agent writes and evolves over the dialogue (the Memory Manager constructs and maintains the bank via ADD/UPDATE/DELETE/NOOP); retrieval at QA time runs over this self-written growing memory bank, not a static external corpus.
completeness_vs_topk_objective: At QA time a fixed top-k is retrieved (60 candidate memories, 30 per participant), then a learned Memory Distillation policy selects a variable-size relevant subset before reasoning, so the effective objective is precision-driven variable-size selection of relevant entries out of a fixed top-k retrieval pool rather than a fixed final-k ranking.
cbr_cycle_coverage: [uncertain] Not framed as CBR. Loosely, mechanisms touch Retrieve (RAG over memory) and Retain (write-back via memory operations), but Reuse/Revise in the case-based sense are not implemented; the work is not positioned as case-based reasoning.
explicit_cbr_grounding: False. The paper does not frame itself as case-based reasoning and does not cite Aamodt & Plaza / Kolodner; it adopts a CRUD-style {ADD, UPDATE, DELETE, NOOP} memory-operation framing (following Mem0) rather than CBR.
retrieval_unit: Single memory entry (a natural-language fact / consolidated statement, e.g. 'Andrew adopted 2 dogs named Buddy and Scout'); these are episodic memory items derived from dialogue turns, not raw token snippets or full trajectories.
index_source: Growing memory bank constructed online over the dialogue stream: at each turn an LLM extracts key info, retrieves related entries, and the RL-fine-tuned Memory Manager updates the store. Training-data construction uses GPT-4o-mini to build temporal memory-bank snapshots from preceding turns. The bank evolves during processing rather than being a frozen offline corpus.
index_structure_topology: Flat memory bank of fact entries keyed by ID, retrieved via similarity-based (vector) RAG; entries are maintained per-participant (memories segmented by speaker/user). No knowledge-graph or hierarchical index is used (contrasts with graph-based memory systems like A-Mem/Zep).
retriever_type: Dense similarity-based RAG retriever (off-the-shelf semantic similarity retrieval over memory entries). [uncertain] The specific embedding model / retriever backbone is not explicitly named in the main text.
retriever_learning_signal: None for the retriever itself (the RAG retriever is off-the-shelf and not trained). The learned components are the Memory Manager and Answer Agent policies, trained with outcome-driven RL (downstream answer Exact Match reward). The Answer Agent's Memory Distillation acts as a learned post-retrieval selection policy, but the underlying similarity retriever is fixed.
query_construction: At QA time the raw question is used as the query to retrieve candidate memories (top-30 per participant). During memory construction, the newly extracted/summarized information from the current dialogue turn serves as the query/key to retrieve related existing memories for the Memory Manager.
query_granularity: Two levels: (1) turn/step-level during memory construction (extracted info from the current turn queries the bank to drive ADD/UPDATE/DELETE/NOOP), and (2) task/question-level at QA time (the question retrieves candidate memories once before answering).
when_to_retrieve: Memory-construction retrieval is per-turn (iterative, fixed schedule as each dialogue turn arrives). QA-time retrieval is one-shot per question (retrieve 60 candidates once, then distill and answer).
retrieval_trigger_signal: Fixed schedule: retrieval is triggered deterministically at every dialogue turn (for memory management) and once per question (for answering). There is no learned/uncertainty-based trigger for WHEN to retrieve; the learned policies decide WHAT operation to apply and WHICH retrieved memories to use, not whether to retrieve.
reranking: No dedicated reranker stage in the main pipeline. The paper explicitly compares against a Base+Reranker pipeline as an ablation and argues its learned Memory Distillation achieves higher accuracy with lower latency than reranker-based pipelines, positioning distillation as a substitute for reranking.
retrieved_context_refinement: Learned Memory Distillation: the Answer Agent pre-selects (filters) the most relevant entries from the 60 retrieved candidates before reasoning, discarding distractors/noise. This is an LLM-driven, RL-fine-tuned relevance-filtering / distillation step (not classic rerank or compression).
tool_document_engineering: N/A (no tool/skill retrieval; memory entries are LLM-generated fact summaries, not tool docstrings).
index_content_separation: N/A / No explicit progressive-disclosure index-then-content separation; memory entries themselves are lightweight fact statements stored and retrieved directly.
dynamic_index_and_protocol: N/A (no tool index / external API protocol; memory store is the agent's own evolving bank).
how_retrieved_used: Prompt augmentation with distilled memories: retrieved memories are filtered by the Memory Distillation policy and the selected relevant entries are concatenated with the question to form a memory-augmented prompt over which the Answer Agent reasons to produce the answer. RL outcome reward (answer EM) also serves as a training signal for both the manager and answer policies.
planning_integration: Two-stage pipeline: Stage 1 (retrieve-then-manage) maintains/evolves the memory bank turn-by-turn via the Memory Manager; Stage 2 (retrieve-then-distill-then-answer) is plan-then-act at QA time, where memories are retrieved once, distilled, then reasoned over to answer. No tree search / MCTS; integration is sequential per question.
reasoning_search_interleaving_granularit: Per-answer at QA time (single retrieval + distillation + reasoning pass per question, with the Answer Agent first outputting selected memories then the answer). Memory-management retrieval/operations are per-turn during bank construction.
adaptation_mechanism: N/A (not a CBR case-adaptation method). The closest analog is RL-fine-tuned reuse: the Memory Manager learns to consolidate overlapping info via UPDATE rather than DELETE+ADD, and the Answer Agent learns to distill and reason; both adapted via outcome-driven RL (PPO/GRPO), not case revision.
retrieved_item_representation: Structured natural-language note / fact statement (e.g. JSON-tagged memory entries with id, text, and an operation event field such as ADD/UPDATE/DELETE/NONE during management); at answer time the injected form is the distilled set of relevant free-text memory statements with timestamps.
abstraction_level_of_retrieved_unit: Distilled fact/statement-level memory (consolidated natural-language summaries of dialogue content), higher abstraction than raw dialogue turns but not a procedural skill or reusable workflow.
noise_robustness_mechanism: Learned Memory Distillation in the RL-fine-tuned Answer Agent: it filters out irrelevant/distractor memories from the 60 retrieved candidates before reasoning, reducing 'lost in the middle' style distraction. Trained via outcome-driven RL so that selecting/reasoning over noisy retrieval still yields correct answers. Ablation shows distillation improves all metrics.
memory_type: episodic (external memory bank of dialogue-derived fact entries), actively managed via CRUD-style operations.
write_back: True. The Memory Manager writes new experiences into memory via structured operations ADD (insert new entry), UPDATE (consolidate/merge into an existing entry, keeping ID), DELETE (prune contradictory entry), or NOOP (no change).
online_growth: Yes. The memory bank is incrementally built and evolved as new dialogue turns arrive (per-turn ADD/UPDATE/DELETE/NOOP). The store grows/changes during processing rather than being frozen after offline induction.
write_back_trigger: Per-turn: at every new dialogue turn the Memory Manager evaluates the extracted information against retrieved existing memories and issues one of ADD/UPDATE/DELETE/NOOP. Writes are not gated on success/failure of QA; they happen continuously as the dialogue stream is processed (operations are learned via downstream answer-correctness reward, but the trigger to act is per-turn/scheduled).
failure_experience_usage: [uncertain] The memory bank stores consolidated factual content rather than explicit success/failure trajectories. There is no described mechanism for storing failed QA attempts as negative experiences; the DELETE operation prunes contradictory/outdated content. Negative/failure experience storage in the trajectory sense is not used.
memory_evolution_update: Mutable with consolidation: append (ADD), dedup-merge / refine-overwrite (UPDATE consolidates overlapping or more-detailed info while keeping the same ID), and forget-prune (DELETE removes contradictory entries); NOOP leaves entries unchanged. A key behavior learned by RL is to favor UPDATE-style consolidation over fragmenting DELETE+ADD.
retrieval_as_learned_policy: Partly. The candidate retrieval (top-k similarity RAG) is a fixed, non-learned step; but the downstream memory-USE policy (Answer Agent's Memory Distillation = which retrieved memories to select/reason over) and the memory-management operation policy are learned/RL-optimized (PPO/GRPO with outcome-driven reward). So memory selection/use is a learned policy while initial retrieval is fixed top-k.
cross_agent_or_cross_framework_sharing: No. Single-agent private memory per dialogue; the two agents (Memory Manager, Answer Agent) operate within one framework and the memory bank is not shared across multiple heterogeneous agents/frameworks.
benchmarks: LoCoMo (primary; long multi-session dialogues, ~600 turns / 26k tokens reported in main text, with single-hop, multi-hop, open-domain, temporal questions; adversarial subset excluded; 1:1:8 train/val/test split = 152/81/1307 questions), MSC (Multi-Session Chat, MemGPT-modified version), and LongMemEval (long-term interactive memory benchmark). Models trained only on LoCoMo and evaluated zero-shot on MSC and LongMemEval.
benchmark_family: memory / long-term conversational QA (LoCoMo, MSC, LongMemEval) with multi-hop and temporal reasoning subtypes.
baselines: (1) LoCoMo (RAG) chunk-retrieval baseline; (2) A-Mem (agentic structured memory); (3) Mem0 (modular memory with in-context CRUD operations, the most competitive prior baseline); (4) MemoryOS (memory-as-OS framework, strongest non-RL baseline); (5) Memory-SFT (supervised fine-tuning ablation: same architecture/data as Memory-R1 but behavior-cloned from GPT-5-generated trajectories instead of RL). All re-implemented on LLaMA-3.1-8B-Instruct and Qwen-2.5-7B-Instruct backbones (temperature 0, max 2048 tokens).
key_metrics: Token-level F1 (F1), BLEU-1 (B1) for lexical overlap, and LLM-as-a-Judge (J) for semantic correctness (CORRECT/WRONG labeling). Also reports inference latency (median and tail) in the distillation-vs-reranking comparison.
headline_result: On LoCoMo with LLaMA-3.1-8B-Instruct, Memory-R1-GRPO sets a new state of the art, with relative improvements over the strongest baseline (MemoryOS) of +28.5% F1, +34.0% BLEU-1, and +30.2% LLM-as-a-Judge (overall scores 45.02 F1 / 37.51 B1 / 62.74 J), achieved with only 152 training QA pairs. (Note: abstract/intro phrase the gain over 'Mem0' as ~28% F1 / 34% BLEU-1 / 30% J; main-results text attributes the same percentages to MemoryOS as the strongest baseline.)
ablations: Component ablations (Figure 5) removing each piece on LLaMA-3.1-8B: (a) without RL-fine-tuned Memory Manager, PPO drops from 41.0/32.9/57.5 to 34.5/28.1/49.0 (GRPO to 37.5/30.6/52.9); (b) without RL-fine-tuned Answer Agent, PPO is 32.5/24.6/59.4 and GRPO 33.0/24.9/59.9 vs full 41.0/32.9/57.5 (PPO) and 45.0/37.5/62.7 (GRPO); (c) without Memory Distillation, PPO 39.3/30.9/57.4 -> 41.0/32.9/57.5, GRPO 41.0/34.4/60.1 -> 45.0/37.5/62.7. Stronger Memory Manager compounds Answer Agent gains (GPT-4o-mini manager vs LLaMA manager: F1 +19.72 vs +10.10, B1 +18.19 vs +10.81, J +15.76 vs +5.05). Reward-design ablation (Table 2): PPO with J-based reward yields highest J (63.58) but lower F1/B1 (33.69/23.36) due to verbose answers, while EM-based reward gives balanced 41.05/32.91/57.54; EM reward chosen. PPO vs GRPO: GRPO converges faster initially, both reach comparable final reward.
evaluation_decoupling: No. Only end-to-end QA metrics (F1/BLEU-1/LLM-as-a-Judge) are reported; intrinsic retrieval metrics such as Recall@k or nDCG for the memory retrieval/distillation are not reported separately.
process_vs_outcome_metrics: Primarily outcome (final-answer) metrics. Process quality is illustrated qualitatively via case studies (correct UPDATE vs erroneous DELETE+ADD operations; distilled-memory selection) and component ablations, but there are no quantitative step-wise memory-operation-accuracy or retrieval-faithfulness metrics.
cost_efficiency_tradeoff: Data efficiency is the headline: strong gains with only 152 training QA pairs. Memory Distillation vs reranking comparison (Figure 8) shows Memory-R1 (GRPO) achieves higher accuracy with lower median and tail latency than a Base+Reranker pipeline, which adds substantial latency for modest accuracy gains. Training: 4x NVIDIA H100 80GB GPUs (8 for Qwen-2.5-14B), total batch size 128, micro-batch 2/GPU, max prompt/response 4096/2048 tokens. No explicit API-cost or per-query retrieval-call counts beyond the fixed 60-candidate retrieval.
context_budget_and_selection_count: Retrieval pool fixed at 60 candidate memories per question (top-30 most relevant per participant, 2 participants). The Answer Agent then distills to a variable, smaller relevant subset before answering (precision-driven). Max prompt length 4096 tokens, max response 2048 tokens; answers constrained to be short (~5-6 words per prompt). Memory-construction temporal bank built from preceding turns ([uncertain]: text variously cites 24 turns and 50 turns; Algorithm 1 says previous 50 turns, the data-construction prose says 24 turns).
benchmark_construction_and_size: N/A (not a benchmark paper). Uses existing benchmarks; LoCoMo evaluation split is 152/81/1307 (train/val/test) questions after excluding the adversarial subset.
builds_on: Mem0 (Chhikara et al., 2025) memory-operation set {ADD, UPDATE, DELETE, NOOP} and RAG-style 60-candidate retrieval setup; PPO (Schulman et al., 2017) and GRPO (Shao et al., 2024) RL algorithms; VERL / HybridFlow RLHF framework (Sheng et al., 2025) for training; LoCoMo benchmark (Maharana et al., 2024); RL-for-LLM-behavior line including Search-R1 (Jin et al., 2025), ToolRL (Qian et al., 2025), R1-Searcher (Song et al., 2025). Backbones: LLaMA-3.1-8B-Instruct and Qwen-2.5-3B/7B/14B-Instruct.
contrasts_with: Static, heuristic-driven memory pipelines that use vanilla in-context LLMs to choose memory operations without a correctness-tied learning signal: Mem0, MemGPT (Packer et al., 2023), A-Mem (Xu et al., 2025), MemoryOS, MemLLM (Modarressi et al., 2024); and reranker-based retrieval pipelines (Base+Reranker). Also contrasts with supervised imitation (Memory-SFT distilled from GPT-5) by showing outcome-driven RL outperforms behavior cloning.
lineage: Belongs to the decision/experience-memory + RL sub-topic (group F, decision_memory_rl): casts external-memory management and memory utilization as RL-optimized policies (PPO/GRPO) over a growing episodic memory bank, extending the RL-for-LLM-agents lineage (Search-R1, ToolRL, R1-Searcher, WebAgent-R1) to the memory-management problem; among the first to frame memory operation selection and relevant-memory utilization as an RL problem.
